content: States must prohibit all forms of forced abortion, as outlined in the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) General Comment No. 3 (2016). 15 (2013). This includes allowing children to consent to certain medical treatments, such as safe abortion, without requiring parental or guardian consent. Public funding should subsidize primary healthcare services, including legal abortion, ensuring affordability and free access for economically disadvantaged women. States must provide appropriate SRH care to address sexual violence against women and girls, including access to abortion in cases of rape or incest, as stated in the Human Rights Committee (HRC) General Comment No. 36 (2018). Barriers to abortion in cases of sexual violence, such as requiring proof of legal proceedings, must be removed. Post-abortion care must be available in all circumstances, even where abortion is illegal. This care must be unconditional and not dependent on a woman’s cooperation with criminal investigations. Healthcare providers must not be required to report women seeking abortion-related care to law enforcement. Post-abortion care must also remain confidential and cannot be used as evidence in legal proceedings against women or abortion providers. Denial of abortion, healthcare, and bereavement support in cases of fatal fetal diagnoses can amount to cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment, violating the right to be free from torture. Laws regulating abortion must be evidence-based and proportionate to protect the right to health. Criminalization of abortion violates international human rights law (IHRL) and perpetuates unsafe conditions. States must decriminalize abortion and repeal laws that impede access to SRH services, such as mandatory waiting periods or third-party consent requirements. Healthcare providers offering abortion care must be protected from harassment, violence, and intimidation. Women and girls seeking abortion must be protected from stigma and discrimination. At a minimum, abortion must be available, accessible, and of good quality in cases where the life or health of the woman is at risk, in cases of rape or incest, and in situations involving severe or fatal fetal impairments. The right to sexual and reproductive health requires states to refrain from interfering with individuals’ exercise of this right. This includes reforming laws that criminalize abortion and ensuring access to safe, legal, and effective abortion services.
